# Tracked checkout declaration (v1)

Schema for `.tera/tracked-checkouts/<name>.hcl` declarations per [ADR-150](../adr/ADR-150-a-knowledge-base-is-a-repository-and-a-plugin.md) D11. A **tracked checkout** is one ref of a repository that a host keeps as read-only trees, one immutable tree per commit, to be mounted into a sandbox: the system vault declares the repository, whose credential reads it, and which ref it follows. A mount holds one commit for its whole life; nothing rewrites a tree under a reader.

**Only the system vault's declarations count.** A checkout carries a choice of read credential, so it is deployment configuration. In any other vault, `.tera/tracked-checkouts/` is the contribute ability `vaults/contribute/tracked-checkouts`, which no deployment profile admits by default — not `dev` or `embedded`, whose default admits an ordinary contribute ability, and not `server` — and which the `repository` role the binary contributes never names: its files are refused at mount, naming the ability and the binding that would grant it, and at `config plan` with `kind_not_allowed`, unless a system-vault `role_binding` grants that ability to the vault's principal explicitly. Any system-vault grant that matches the ability counts as explicit, wildcards included: a role granting `vaults/contribute/#`, `vaults/contribute/+`, `vaults/#` or `#`, bound to `vault:<alias>` or `vault:*`, admits `tracked-checkouts`, a credential-bearing ability, under every profile — so a "contribute everything" role bound to a vault's principal grants it too. Admission is not loading: even granted, a checkout another vault carries is not part of the declared set.

**Three ref modes, exactly one per declaration**, spelled exactly as a `tracked_vault`'s: `branch "<name>" {}` follows a branch's head; `tags "<pattern>" {}` follows the highest matching tag by semver, optionally only tags whose GitHub release is published (`release {}`) and with prereleases in or out; `pin "<ref>" {}` holds exactly one tag or commit, which is how a freeze or a rollback is done.

**The credential is named, never written.** `worker` and `connection` name the worker whose credential for that connection reads the repository (ADR-148 D3). The worker must exist and bind the connection, and the connection must be declared in the system vault; each is refused at load and at plan otherwise. The daemon resolves the credential itself, and it never enters a sandbox, a refusal or a plan.

**Synced when mounted.** Taking a mount first brings the checkout to the commit its ref resolves to on the remote at that moment, then holds that commit's tree for the mount's life. So there is **no `poll_interval`**: a checkout is brought current whenever it is mounted and has nothing to poll for. There is **no size limit**: the trees are bounded by the host's sizing of the store that holds them, never per declaration. There is **no `path`**: a checkout is the whole repository. Each of the three is refused as an attribute the kind does not have.

The file stem is the checkout's name, so `handbook.hcl` declares the checkout `handbook`; the name is the segment of the resource `tracked-checkouts/<name>` that mounting it is authorized as `invoke` on. The recipe declares a single `tracked_checkout` block whose label is optional and, if written, must equal that stem.

## Example

A minimal `tracked-checkout`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/tracked-checkouts/example-tracked-checkout.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

tracked_checkout "example-tracked-checkout" {
  repository = "https://git.example.com/acme/handbook.git"
  worker     = "example-worker"
  connection = "example-connection"

  branch "main" {}
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | — | — | const `v1` | Per-recipe grammar version. Required; this schema applies when version is v1. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The checkout's name (the HCL block label). Optional: the filename stem is the identity, so a label, if written, must equal it. It is the segment of the resource tracked-checkouts/<name> a role grants invoke on to mount it, and what each host keys the checkout's trees under, so it carries no / or \, no ACL wildcard (*, + or #), no whitespace, and does not begin with a dot. |
| `description` | string | no | — | — | — | One line for people. |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The repository, as an absolute https:// URL with a host and a path (https://github.com/acme/handbook.git), spelled exactly as a tracked_vault spells it. It carries no user or password: the read credential is the worker's connection, presented over HTTPS, so http://, ssh://, git@ and file:// URLs are refused. With release {} it must be a repository the GitHub API can address, whose path is /<owner>/<repo> with an optional .git suffix. |
| `worker` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The worker whose credential reads the repository, and makes the release lookup. A checkout has no filer, so the worker is named outright. It must be declared, and must bind a credential for connection with a connection block of its own (ADR-148 D3); a declaration naming a worker that does not is refused at load and at plan. The credential's value is never written here, and never reaches a sandbox, a refusal or a plan. |
| `connection` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | Which of the worker's credentials reads the repository: the name of a .tera/connections/<name>.hcl recipe the system vault declares, refused at load and at plan when it is not. |
| `branch` | block | no | — | — | — | Follow a branch: its head is live, and every move is applied through plan and apply. Labelled with the branch name, without refs/heads/. Exactly one of branch, tags and pin. |
| `tags` | block | no | — | — | — | Follow tags matching a pattern: the highest matching tag by semver that passes the filters is live. Exactly one of branch, tags and pin. |
| `pin` | block | no | — | — | — | Pin a ref: exactly that tag or commit is live. Rollback and freezing are pins, set here and removed once a fixed tag exists. Exactly one of branch, tags and pin. |

**Exactly one of** `branch` | `tags` | `pin`.

## `branch` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The branch's name, without refs/heads/ (the HCL block label). |

## `tags` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The tag pattern (the HCL block label): a literal prefix and one trailing *, with no other *, ?, [ or backslash. A tag matches when it begins with the prefix, and its version is what follows; when the prefix ends in v, that v is given back to the version, so config-v* and config-* both read config-v1.2.3 as v1.2.3. The version must be a full semver: a matching tag that is not is reported and skipped, never guessed at. |
| `prereleases` | boolean | no | `false` | — | — | Whether a prerelease is a candidate: a tag whose version has a semver prerelease part, or, with release {}, whose GitHub release is marked prerelease. Default false. |
| `release` | block | no | — | — | — | Require a GitHub release for the tag that is published and is not a draft. Absent, a tag needs no release. A release lookup is made only for a new matching tag above what is live, and a tag whose release is absent or a draft is looked up again at most once per interval, so publishing the release later applies the tag. |

## `tags.release` block

Nested under `tags`.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `api_url` | string | no | `https://api.github.com` | — | — | The GitHub REST API root the release lookup calls, as an absolute https:// URL. Set it for GitHub Enterprise Server. |

## `pin` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The pinned ref (the HCL block label): a full commit id - exactly 40 or 64 lowercase hex characters - or else a tag name. An abbreviated commit id is a tag name that will not resolve. A branch cannot be pinned. |
